terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to see the market lists made from the shelf.

tasks.title: Round prices for the market
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/map-filter-find.js`, first write a function of your own, `roundUp(cents)`: it returns `cents` rounded up to the next whole 100, so `1250` becomes `1300` and `1800` stays `1800`. It only helps `marketPrices`, so it stays off the export line.

Then make `marketPrices(prices)` return a new list with every price rounded up, in the same order. Use `map` and `roundUp`.

Check calls `roundUp` with prices of its own, a whole 100 included, then `marketPrices` with lists of its own, an empty one included. It makes sure the list handed in has not changed and that `marketPrices` uses `map` and `roundUp`.
nextSteps: Write `roundUp` above `marketPrices`, from its name to its closing brace.
In `marketPrices`, give back what `map` makes when it uses `roundUp` on each price.
Run the file: every price on the first line should end in 00.
hints: Rounding up to a whole 100 is rounding up a number of hundreds. You met the rounding that always goes up in the issue on numbers.
Divide by 100, round that up with `Math.ceil`, and multiply by 100 again. `map` calls the function you give it once per price and puts each answer in a new list.

tasks.title: Fill the cheap table
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, make `cheapTable(prices, limit)` return a new list of the prices below `limit`, in their order. A price of exactly `limit` does not go on the cheap table. Use `filter`.

Check calls `cheapTable` with prices and limits of its own: a price equal to the limit, a limit above every price, one below every price, and an empty list. It also makes sure the list handed in has not changed.
nextSteps: Write the question to ask about one price: is it below `limit`?
Hand that question to `filter` and give back the list it makes.
Run the file and try another limit in the demo line.
hints: `filter` keeps an item when the function you give it says true for it. So that function is a question about one price.
The question uses `limit`, which the arrow function can see because it is written inside `cheapTable`. Below means the equal case is left out.
The body is one line: `return prices.filter((cents) => cents < limit)`.

tasks.title: Find a scent by its letter
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make `firstStartingWith(scents, letter)` return the first scent of `scents` whose first letter is `letter`, or `'None'` when no scent starts with it. Use `find`.

Check calls `firstStartingWith` with lists and letters of its own: two scents with the same letter, a scent with the letter later in its name, a letter no scent has, and an empty list.
nextSteps: Write the question about one scent: is its first character `letter`?
Hand it to `find`, and keep what comes back in a `const`.
Give back that scent, or `'None'` when `find` found nothing, and run the file.
hints: `filter` gives back a list of every match. The task asks for one scent, and another list tool stops at the first match and gives back the item itself.
`scent[0]` is the first character of a text. When nothing matches, `find` gives back `undefined`, and `??`, which you met with `null` and `undefined`, can step in for it.
`const found = scents.find((scent) => scent[0] === letter)`, then `return found ?? 'None'`.

tasks.title: Print the small tags
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, make `tagsFor(scents)` return a new list of the scents that fit on a tag, each in capital letters, in their order. A tag fits 8 characters at most, spaces included: `'Lavender'` fits as `'LAVENDER'`, `'Smoked fig'` is left out. Use `filter` and `map`.

Check calls `tagsFor` with lists of its own: a scent of exactly 8 characters, scents with spaces, a list where nothing fits, and an empty list. It also makes sure the list handed in has not changed.
nextSteps: Decide which of the two jobs is `filter` and which is `map`.
Keep the scents that fit, counting their characters with `length`.
Turn each kept scent into capital letters.
Give back the final list and run the file.
hints: There are two jobs: keep some scents, and change each one. Each of the two list tools from the lesson does one of them.
`filter` gives back a list, so you can call `map` straight on its answer. At most 8 includes 8 itself. `toUpperCase()` turns text into capital letters.
